stem: Which principle means that the government, the police and ordinary people must all obey the same laws?
explanation: Under the rule of law nobody is above the law, including people in power.
source: Handbook ch. 1 · The values and principles of the UK

stem: Which of these are part of the United Kingdom? Select TWO.
explanation: Wales and Northern Ireland are two of the UK's four countries. The Isle of Man is a Crown dependency and Ireland is independent.
source: Handbook ch. 2 · What is the UK?

stem: In which English county is Stonehenge?
explanation: Stonehenge stands in Wiltshire, in south-west England.

stem: At which battle in 1314 did the Scots defeat the English?
explanation: Robert the Bruce led the Scots to victory over the English at Bannockburn in 1314.

stem: Which of Henry VIII's wives were executed? Select TWO.
explanation: Anne Boleyn and her cousin Catherine Howard were both executed. Jane Seymour died after childbirth and Catherine Parr outlived Henry.
source: Handbook ch. 3 · The Tudors and Stuarts

stem: Why did George I rely heavily on his ministers?
options: He was too young to rule
explanation: George I spoke little English, so his ministers took on more of the work of government.

stem: Which Minister for Health led the setting up of the NHS?
explanation: Aneurin Bevan, Minister for Health, led the creation of the NHS in 1948.

stem: Which flower is associated with Wales?
explanation: The daffodil is the flower of Wales. The thistle is Scotland's, the rose England's and the shamrock Northern Ireland's.
source: Handbook ch. 4 · Leisure; Places of interest

stem: Which statement about British democracy is correct?
options: It developed gradually over many years
It was introduced all at once after a revolution
It was copied from the French constitution
It began only after the Second World War
explanation: Britain's democracy grew step by step, as the right to vote was gradually widened.
source: Handbook ch. 5 · British democracy and the government

stem: Civil servants are politically neutral and are chosen on merit.
explanation: Civil servants are not political appointees. They are selected on merit and must stay neutral.
source: Handbook ch. 5 · Devolution; The UK and the world
